title: One simulated machine step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $o$ be an oracle for two languages on Boolean words. Suppose that, for every $i\le |v|$, the first oracle answer on the encoding of $x$ paired with the binary expansion of $i$ is true exactly when $i<|v|$, and, for every $i<|v|$, the second oracle answer on that encoding equals the $i$-th bit of $v$ (defaulting to false if absent). Let $c$ be a live configuration of $M$ on $v$, and let $d$ represent $c$ in the compiled program. If every work-tape head of $c$ and of its next machine configuration lies in $[-S,S]$, then the compiled program, started at $d$, reaches after some finite number $N$ of steps a configuration representing the next configuration of $M$; every configuration strictly before step $N$ satisfies the safety bounds for length $|v|$ and parameter $S$.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle on two indices and Boolean words
The first oracle-answer condition for every $i\le |v|`
The second oracle-answer condition for every $i<|v|`
A configuration $c$ of $M$ on $v$ with nonhalting state
All work-tape heads in both $c$ and its next configuration lie in $[-S,S]`
